name: Keppel
lede: Keppel is a cool teal-green that has been in use as a color name only since 2001, with no tie back to the older surname it shares.

sections.title: A 2001 web color, an older surname
sections.body:
Our color library dates the name Keppel to 2001, when it was listed on the Xona.com Color List, one of several unofficial web color dictionaries from that era [1]. Keppel is also an old British and Dutch surname, traced further back to a Latin word for a hooded cape, *cappa*, and originally an occupational name for someone who made them [2]. Nothing in our sources ties the 2001 color name to that older family name; we treat any connection as undocumented rather than assume one [1][2].

The nearest named neighbor by measured color is [[tyrolite-green]], duller than this shade; [[keppel]] sits close by, more vivid [3]. [[persian-green]] and [[zomp]] are a little further out [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a match for Keppel in 3 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.01 percent, rarer than 82 percent of the named colors we track, as photographed [4]. Clean teals this cool and this saturated are uncommon across the whole archive, so a count this small is not unusual for the family [4]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications [4].

origin.named_after: undocumented as a color name beyond the 2001 Xona.com Color List; unrelated to the older Keppel surname

notes.cite: ColorHub archive (23,781 paintings), computed match, as photographed

questions.q: Where was the name Keppel first listed as a color, according to our sources?
True or false: our sources confirm this color name comes from the old Keppel family surname.

openers: Keppel the color is barely 25 years old, despite sharing a name with a centuries-old family.
